metadata.title: Results from TALIS Starting Strong 2024: Strengthening early childhood education and care, TALIS, OECD Publishing, Paris, https://doi.org/10.1787/789306ff-en

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: TALIS Starting Strong 2024 is based on questionnaires administered to ECEC staff and setting leaders, aiming for representative samples within each participating country or subnational entity at the relevant ECEC level (ISCED 02 for ages 3–6, and additional settings for children under age 3). The note reports indicator percentages and comparisons across countries/subnational entities, but it does not specify the exact sampling-weight variables or replicate-weight procedures used in the underlying database. Because this is a descriptive OECD results note rather than a student-level achievement modeling study, the analysis is presented as survey-based estimates of shares (e.g., staff participation in training, leader feedback frequency) and is subject to non-response bias risk, as indicated in the figure notes. Analysts should consult the TALIS Starting Strong 2024 technical documentation/database for the precise complex survey design variables and any replicate-weight method (if applicable) used to compute standard errors and confidence intervals.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This note reports descriptive indicators from self-reports (staff and leaders) rather than cognitive achievement outcomes with plausible values. As a result, plausible values are not applicable to the reported indicators. The document also does not describe any missing-data handling procedure for questionnaire non-response, so the missing-data strategy cannot be assessed from the provided text; this is a reporting gap for methodological transparency.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The note focuses on TALIS Starting Strong 2024 ECEC settings in Colombia, covering (i) public and private service providers of the second cycle of initial education in the comprehensive care framework (preescolar escolarizado y escuela tradicional pública y privada) serving children age 3–6, and (ii) the initial education service of the Colombian Institute of Family Welfare (Hogares Comunitarios de Bienestar familiares and Hogares Comunitarios de Bienestar institucionales) serving children age 0–6. For the cross-country comparisons shown in the note, the survey targets representative samples of staff and leaders for each participating country/subnational entity at the pre-primary level (ISCED 02) and additionally includes settings for children under age 3 in selected entities.

data.outcome_summary: TALIS Starting Strong 2024 is an OECD large-scale survey collecting self-reported questionnaire data from early childhood education and care (ECEC) staff and setting leaders, with the Colombia note summarizing initial findings across three themes: quality for children and families, workforce retention, and system foundations. The note reports descriptive indicators such as staff time in direct contact with children, participation in job-embedded training and collaborative learning, leader feedback frequency, family engagement practices, and sources of work stress and intended turnover. It also provides comparisons with other participating countries and subnational entities at ISCED 02 (pre-primary) and, for some entities, settings for children under age 3. The document does not present student-level predictive modeling, plausible values, or ML performance metrics; therefore, no ML-based causal or predictive conclusions can be drawn. Estimates are flagged as potentially affected by non-response bias in figure notes.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a descriptive OECD results note for TALIS Starting Strong 2024 rather than an empirical ML study. It does not report an analytic sample size (students/staff/leaders), country-level Ns, plausible values, missing-data handling procedures, or any predictive modeling pipeline. Consequently, fields related to ML techniques and structured predictive findings are intentionally left empty, while the survey design and indicator-based results are summarized narratively.
